summary.text: Check the number in ScamShield. A single report does not mark it as scam. Call 1799 if it was wrongly marked.

details.heading: One report is not enough
details.body: A single report does not automatically mark a phone number as scam. If the number is legitimate, you do not need to worry.

steps.name: Check the number
steps.text: Use ScamShield's Check for Scams feature to check the phone number.

steps.name: Read the result
steps.text: A red result saying “Beware, this looks like a scam” means the number is blocked. “Be careful, we're not sure about this one” means it has not been marked as scam or blocked.

steps.name: Request an unblock
steps.text: If you believe the number was wrongly marked as scam, call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.

sources.page_title: What should I do if I accidentally reported a number as scam?

quotes.text: Please be assured that a single report alone does not automatically mark a phone number as a scam.
If you've accidentally reported a number as "scam", you may use the Check for Scams feature to check if the phone number is marked as scam in the ScamShield database.
A phone number is only blocked if the check outcome appears red with the message "Beware, this looks like a scam."
If you believe a phone number has been wrongly marked as scam, please reach out to the ScamShield Helpline at 1799 to request an unblock.
If this is a legitimate phone number, you don't need to worry. The phone number won't be incorrectly marked as a scam based on a single report.
